first_hunter_context.bar: Q3 2026 consensus revenue $4.20M, EPS -$0.97, from one source only: MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/LENZ/earnings/ (read 2026-10-28). The company gives no guidance. There is no second agreeing estimate source, so every finding that depends on the bar is capped small. The line the stock actually trades on (VIZZ monthly packs and product revenue; Q2 was ~27,000 packs and $1.74M) has no sourced consensus. My estimate: Q3 product revenue ~$2.0-2.6M plus the $0.8M Arrotex license recognised in July gives total ~$2.8-3.4M, about 25% under the $4.2M headline bar.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: FINRA short interest via equibles.com (https://equibles.com/stocks/lenz/shortinterest, read 2026-10-28): 9,095,817 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 11.81 days to cover. That is down from 10,560,869 on 2026-09-30 and 11.86M on 2026-07-15, so shorts are covering into the print. It is ~29% of the 31.42M shares outstanding; MarketBeat puts it at 31.57% of float. No usable option chain (ATM legs not two-sided), so no skew. Put/call OI is 0.53 on only 275 contracts total, which carries no information. Holders: FMR cut its stake from ~11.8% (Feb 2026) to 5.7% (1,783,202 shares) as of 2026-08-31 (13G/A filed 2026-09-08). BlackRock Portfolio Management filed a new 5.2% 13G (event date 2026-09-30, filed 2026-10-27). Millennium is at 3.7% (13G/A filed 2026-10-21). No Form 4 insider filings since July.

evidence.text: License revenue falls in Q3, so headline revenue and EPS likely miss MarketBeat's single-source bar. The 10-Q's subsequent-events note documents only $0.8M of Arrotex license revenue recognised in July 2026, against $3.75M in Q2 (a $2.5M Théa milestone plus $1.25M Everest sublicense). With product revenue of ~$2.0-2.6M, total Q3 revenue comes to ~$2.8-3.4M against $4.20M consensus. With SG&A at or above Q2's $39.4M (117 territories deployed by end-Q2, national TV live from July 6), the net loss per share likely lands around -$1.05 to -$1.20 against a -$0.97 consensus.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 (reported 2026-03-24) missed revenue ($1.59M vs $3.09M) and EPS (-$1.16 vs -$0.91); stock -17.9%. Q1 2026 missed EPS (-$1.32 vs -$1.10); -20.8%. Q2 2026 headline revenue beat ($5.49M vs $2.38M, mostly license); only -3.3%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The MarketBeat $4.2M figure only makes sense if it carries license revenue resembling Q2's. If the market had priced a ~$3M total, the published consensus would sit near $3M. The bar has one source, and buy-side models probably already strip license timing, so the size is capped.
evidence.independence: The Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001815776/000181577626000051/a991q226pressrelease.htm) itemises Q2 license revenue as $2.5M Théa plus $1.25M Everest, both one-time events. It is the same company, so this is not independent; it is the comparison base.

evidence.text: Script momentum entering Q3. On the Q2 call (2026-08-11), management said total VIZZ prescriptions rose more than 45% month over month in July, after telehealth (live 2026-07-06, $35 visit) and national TV launched, with all channels up. Q2 packs grew only ~9% q/q (~27,000). If August-September held even part of the July step-up, Q3 packs would be ~33-38k, product revenue ~$2.1-2.5M, and sequential growth 25-45%, a visible acceleration.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has sold its prints: 6 of the last 8 reactions were negative. The Q2 print carried the +45% July data and still fell 3.3%, then the stock fell another ~40% through September-October.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public since August, yet the stock has fallen from ~$5 to $3.14 since. The market is pricing the July spike as non-recurring (management itself said one month is not a trend). Had it priced sustained acceleration, the stock would not sit at ~0.55x estimated cash. What is unpriced is whether August-September held, and no IQVIA/Symphony series exists: management called retail tracking poor and ~60% of volume goes through ePharmacy.
evidence.independence: The Fierce Healthcare telehealth launch piece (https://www.fiercehealthcare.com/telehealth/lenz-therapeutics-rolls-out-telehealth-offering-presbyopia-drops-vizz) confirms the channel and the $35 fee via Leerink, but carries no volume data. No independent script series was found.

evidence.text: Capital-allocation decision due with the print, on a stock at about half its cash. On the Q2 call, management said it would use Q3 data to decide which initiatives to keep and how much to invest in the next launch phase, and that it needs 'even more discipline in how we allocate capital'. Cash was $220.0M at 2026-06-30, against six-month operating cash use of $72.3M. On ~$35M of Q3 burn, Sep-30 cash would be ~$185M (~$5.9/share) against a ~$99M market cap at $3.14, so a cut in DTC or sales spend has a large asymmetric payoff. Continued full spend would confirm the burn the price already discounts.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior spending-reset print at this company. 2026 prints that carried higher spend and weak launch metrics fell 17.9% and 20.8%.
evidence.why_not_priced: An EV of roughly -$85M means the market is valuing the remaining cash as if most of it will be spent on the launch. If it expected a cost reset, the stock would trade nearer cash. The decision has not been announced: no 8-K since July, no WARN or layoff reports found, and the 10-Q still says SG&A 'will continue to increase in 2026'. The direction is inference, so the range is wide.
evidence.independence: The cash and burn figures come from the 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001815776/000181577626000052/lenz-20260630.htm), a different document from the call quote. The 10-Q's language ('SG&A will continue to increase in 2026') cuts the other way, so this finding is sized net of it.

evidence.text: Crowded short covering into the print. FINRA short interest is 9.10M shares at 2026-10-15 (~29% of 31.42M shares outstanding; 31.6% of float per MarketBeat), with 11.8 days to cover on ~770-890k average volume. Short interest fell 13.9% from 10.56M on 2026-09-30 and 23% from 11.86M in mid-July. The stock sits at its 52-week low, ~0.55x estimated cash, with no ATM capacity left: the TD Cowen $150M ATM was fully used by 2025-12-31.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Short interest was ~21% of float in 2025 and 29-36% in 2026, and the stock still fell on most prints. The squeeze mechanism has not paid here so far; covering has accompanied the decline.
evidence.why_not_priced: Positioning is the information set more than a hidden fact. What matters is that 11.8 days to cover against a below-cash price means any non-negative print forces covering, while a bad print has little fresh supply left: FMR already halved to 5.7% by Aug 31 and the ATM is exhausted.
evidence.independence: MarketBeat short-interest page (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/LENZ/short-interest/): 31.57% of float, 11.81 days to cover, down 13.87%. Same FINRA data underneath, so not independent.

evidence.text: Competition through Q3. Tenpoint's Yuvezzi (carbachol/brimonidine) became available nationwide on 2026-03-30 and launched its first national DTC campaign on 2026-06-29, the same quarter as LENZ's national TV push. LENZ's own 10-Q added Yuvezzi, generic Vuity and Qlosi to its competition risk factor. Shared consumer attention could have damped VIZZ's August-September growth.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print has been attributed to a competitor.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a proxy: no Yuvezzi sales data exists and Tenpoint is private. The launch is public, so it is mostly priced; it is filed small for completeness.
evidence.independence: Yuvezzi availability release (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260330960621/en/YUVEZZI-from-Tenpoint-Therapeutics-Ltd.-Is-Now-Available-Nationwide-Across-the-United-States), a different document.

evidence.text: Greater China approval of aceclidine (Everest Medicines, which took over Corxel's rights on 2026-06-07) is expected in Q1 2027. LENZ is eligible for up to $85M in remaining regulatory and sales milestones.
EU MAA (validated March 2026) and UK MAA (April 2026) are under review. No CHMP opinion is plausible before 2027.
Biopharmawatch site analytics: '15 months runway, $13M monthly burn, lead asset aceclidine+brimonidine Phase 3'
Late-September automated 'stock down 5-7%' write-ups (stock -24.9% month to date)
FMR cut its stake from 11.8% to 5.7% (event 2026-08-31)
Q2 net product revenue +9% q/q reported as unit-based; release arithmetic implies ~5% in dollars
EDGAR filings since 2026-07-01: only the 8-K 5.02 of 2026-07-02 (director Zach Scheiner resigned, no disagreement), the Q2 8-K/10-Q, and three 13G filings; no 8-K since August, no S-3/ATM, no Form 4s
Layoffs / reduction in force / WARN notices for 2026: none found
Analyst actions in October 2026: none found dated; latest seen are the August 2026 BofA downgrade to $7 and Citi's cut to $10
Activist 13D, buyback or strategic-alternatives language: none
Ex-US approvals (Canada/Théa, Korea/Lotus, Saudi) inside the window: none announced
Independent VIZZ script series (IQVIA/Symphony): management calls retail tracking poor; nothing public
Consumer review volume for VIZZ or its telehealth service: nothing found
Yuvezzi sales data: none public
Short-interest settlement 2026-10-30: not yet published

first_hunter_context.bar: No sourced Q3 2026 consensus. Yahoo shows no estimates (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MVIS/analysis), and the Q2 estimate itself was disputed: $3.38m per Benzinga against $1.0m per a MarketBeat preview (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/microvision-mvis-expected-to-announce-quarterly-earnings-on-thursday-2026-07-30/). The only sourced bar is the company's FY2026 revenue guide of $10-15m, reaffirmed 2026-10-07 after Q3 had closed (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/65770/000149315226046140/ex99-1.htm). The Q2 call's prepared remarks said $10-16m, read back in Q&A as $10-15m (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/mvis/transcripts/668269-q2-2026/). H1 revenue was $2.4m (Q1 $0.9m, Q2 $1.5m), so the guide implies $7.6-12.6m in H2. print_vs_bar_pct is my Q3 revenue estimate (~$2.7m) against a pro-rata Q3 share (~$3.0m) of the low end of that implied H2. Because the bar is unsourced, every finding is capped small.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest about 6.2m shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 4.3 days to cover (5.7m and 4.9 days on 09-15), per Curved Trading citing FINRA (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/mvis/short-interest/, seen via search snippet; the page returned 403 to fetch). That is about 20.5% of the 30.15m shares outstanding at 2026-08-14 (per the 13G at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/65770/000205845126000002/primary_doc.xml), so the short is crowded, though part of it is likely a hedge by the convertible-note holder and the warrant holders. No usable option chain, so there is no 25d skew. Put/call OI is 0.77 on 607 contracts total, which is negligible. Tape: spot $1.23, -18% over 20 days, 8.9% above the 52-week low, -93% from the 52-week high. A third-party price table puts the low at $1.08 on 2026-10-19 (https://www.macroaxis.com/microvision-stock-price).

evidence.text: The company reaffirmed FY2026 revenue of $10-15m and guided 2027 revenue to double on 2026-10-07, after Q3 had closed: the CFO said 'we are confident in our ability to meet the full year guidance in the range of $10 million-$15 million', and management said it was 'shipping sensors until the last day of the quarter to maximize revenue'. A guide cut at this print is therefore less likely than the name's history of missed street numbers implies (Q2 revenue $1.47m against a $3.38m estimate).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The reaffirmation itself was sold: a third-party price table shows the stock -13.8% on 4.6m shares on 2026-10-08, the session after the 16:05 ET 8-K. In the baseline, prints that carried guidance (03-04 -29.5%, 05-13 -21.1%) were sold hard; the 08-06 print that reiterated the guide and raised gross margin rose 4.0%.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is public and the stock fell on it, so the statement itself is priced. What may not be priced is that it was made with Q3 already known. If the market believed a hold at the print, the stock would not sit 8.9% off its 52-week low at about $37m market cap against a guide that implies H2 revenue 3-5x H1. The guide sits inside what the company already told the market, so the size is small.
evidence.independence: Q2 call transcript, prepared remarks: 'more revenue coming Q3' from the MicroVision Semiconductor project, and Lake Fusion 'unit sales that are occurring here in Q3' (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/mvis/transcripts/668269-q2-2026/). The investor-update transcript (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/mvis/transcripts/761601-investor-update/) is the same event as the 8-K exhibit and counts once.

evidence.text: The cash runway does not reach year-end without more equity. Cash was $27.2m on 2026-06-30. The $17.0m gross unit offering of 6.8m shares plus 6.8m warrants at $2.50 netted $15.6m on 2026-08-17. Against that sit about $60m of FY2026 burn guidance, of which $35.6m of operating cash was used in H1, and convertible-note redemptions scheduled at $19.8m for the rest of 2026 ($3.0m a month plus a 10% premium). The 10-Q carries going-concern language and a minimum-cash covenant of the lesser of $17.5m or 110% of the note balance. The offering's 45-day lock-up on new issuance and note repayments ended about 2026-10-01, leaving $41.2m of ATM availability. On my walk, Q3-end cash is roughly $25-30m and Q4 needs ATM sales or note conversions into stock, which the Q3 10-Q cover share count will show.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-08-14/17 offering at $2.50 coincided with a reported -40.7% session (search snippet); the stock is now $1.23, below the $2.50 offer and warrant strike. Every print in the baseline after a dilution-heavy quarter was down (03-04 -29.5%, 05-13 -21.1%).
evidence.why_not_priced: The going-concern flag and the August raise are public, and the 69% drawdown since August shows much of this is in the price. What the market cannot yet see is the size of post-lock-up ATM and conversion issuance in October and the Q3-end cash figure against the $17.5m covenant. If that were priced, the stock would trade near the cash-adjusted value with no further drift, rather than having set a new low ($1.08 on 10-19) after the lock-up ended. Rule 4 answer: the money funds operating losses and note redemptions, not a corroborated ramp (H1 revenue $2.4m against $60m of burn), so the sign is negative. It is shrunk for the roughly 20% short interest.
evidence.independence: The offering terms are a separate primary document: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/65770/000149315226038743/form8-k.htm. The Q2 call confirms $41.2m of ATM capacity and the covenant (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/mvis/transcripts/668269-q2-2026/).

evidence.text: Q3 revenue is at risk of landing below whatever street number exists, because the company's own guide is back-loaded. H1 revenue was $2.4m, and the guide needs $7.6-12.6m in H2. On the Q2 call the CEO said MOVIA S has 'not a large revenue portion for 2026' (launched in late October, after Q3) and that IRIS supply was 'more of a timing issue... Q3 or Q4 of this year or Q1 or Q2 of next year'. Q2 revenue missed the $3.38m estimate by 56%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue missed by 56% and the stock rose 4.0% over the print window (08-06), because the guide and the gross-margin raise carried it. Earlier revenue disappointments (03-04, 05-13) were sold 21-30%.
evidence.why_not_priced: No published Q3 consensus exists, so the market has no stated number to be wrong against, and that is why this is capped small. If the back-loading were fully priced, the 10-07 'confident in guidance' statement would not have needed to be made. It is an inference from the company's own phasing comments, not a counted number.
evidence.independence: Benzinga Q2 actual against estimate ($1.47m against $3.38m), via search snippet: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/MVIS/earnings. It partly pulls against finding 1: both rest on the same guide but land on different lines (Q3 actual against FY guide hold).

evidence.text: Management pre-announced balance-sheet actions to be detailed 'in the next few weeks as we come up to our Q3 earnings call': a second phase of operating-expense cuts, a review of 'our debt structure and lease obligations', and 'non-core assets... that we could monetize'. A concrete asset sale, note restructuring or opex number at the print would be the first non-dilutive liquidity source on a going-concern name.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print announced an asset sale or debt restructuring. The 05-13 print, which announced a 15% workforce cut and a burn reduction from $65-70m to $60m, still fell 21.1%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The intention is public. The content (a dollar figure for a monetization or debt amendment) is not, and the stock fell to new lows after the update, so the market has given the intention no credit. If it had, the stock would not have set a new low on 10-19. Sized small because the history shows cost-cut news on this name has not been bought.
evidence.independence: Same event as the 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/65770/000149315226046140/ex99-1.htm), which also mentions evaluating debt structure, leases and non-core asset sales; one source, counted once.

evidence.text: The short is crowded into the print at about 6.2m shares short (2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, 4.3 days to cover), roughly 20% of the 30.15m shares outstanding, while a single individual (Johannes Gnauck / JG Global LLC) disclosed a 7.9% long stake (2.38m shares) on a 13G with event date 2026-09-16. That is a squeeze mechanism on any non-negative surprise in a $37m stock.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline shows only one up print in seven (+4.0% on 08-06); no squeeze on a print is visible in the history.
evidence.why_not_priced: The short is part of the price, but its asymmetry is not: with 4.3 days to cover and borrowable supply competing with ATM issuance, a good-news print would require covering into thin float. Part of the short is likely a hedge by the note and warrant holders and will not cover, which is why this is sized small.
evidence.independence: The short interest figure comes via search snippet (Curved Trading citing FINRA): https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/mvis/short-interest/

evidence.text: Listing risk returns. Spot is $1.23, 23% above the $1 Nasdaq bid floor that MVIS regained compliance with on 2026-08-26, after a 1-for-15 reverse split effective 2026-08-01. Another deficiency needs 30 consecutive sessions below $1, which cannot occur inside this window.

evidence.text: Q3 revenue should land at about $185-188m, roughly 1-3% above the $182.4-183.3m consensus. Q2's $183.6m included $2.8m of one-time revenue (German approval rates and age claims, US deductible, France), so the underlying Q2 run rate is about $180.8m. Q3 has stepped up sequentially in both prior years: +3.1% in 2024 ($150.4m to $155.1m) and +5.3% in 2025 ($158.8m to $167.2m, including $3.3m of FX). Gio active patients were +11% YoY at 4,636. Optune Pax ended Q2 with 285 actives from 418 prescriptions.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue of $183.6m beat the $172.4m consensus by 6.5% with a guide raise, and the stock rose 28.4%. Q1 2026: +27.5%. Q3 2025: $167.2m, stock -4.9%. July 2025: -24.1%. This name has paid for revenue beats lately.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus at $183m equals reported Q2 revenue. The Street has therefore modelled a flat quarter on a base that held $2.8m of one-offs, and has assumed no seasonal step-up and no Pax ramp. If the market expected a clear beat, the stock would not have fallen 9.6% in 20 days back to post-TRIDENT levels while shorts added 1.66m shares.
evidence.independence: The Q3 2025 seasonal step-up comes from a separate document, the Q3 2025 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1645113/000164511325000043/nvcr-20250930xpr1111.htm). The one-time items come from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.ca/news-detail/15276766716830720). The second finding rests on the same Q3 revenue level.

evidence.text: The FY26 guide arithmetic points to a raise. FY $710-725m less H1 $357.7m leaves H2 at $352-367m, or $176-184m a quarter. Management said the high end is 'basically in line with the Q2 results'. A Q3 at or above about $183m leaves Q4 needing only about $169-184m, so at least the low end would likely be lifted.
